note: The strongest suite that runs hermetically for each driver, and how to run it in a temporary copy. `dir` is the driver's directory relative to the repository; `links` are the directories it imports, linked into the copy at the same relative place; `run` is the driver's own suite, in order, run in `dir`; `abi` (Python drivers) is `skynet driver check` through the real python-host against the driver's simulated controller, compared with the outcomes of the unpatched driver. `workspace` (Rust drivers) runs the suite in a disposable copy of the cargo workspace — one per worker, so seeds run in parallel, and the repository is never patched — with `links` copied in as the counterparts the suite runs against. `rung` is F118's: 4 is a counterpart written in this repository, which is all a hermetic suite can be. `{python}` and `{repo}` and `{root}` are substituted; SEED_PYTHON chooses the interpreter, and a suite with `python: NAME` runs under SEED_PYTHON_NAME (requests, spot: the venvs that carry the vendor's client). `requires` (a compiled driver that links a vendor's SDK) names the environment variable that holds the checkout: `--all` skips such a driver, out loud, on a machine without it, and `--driver` runs it and fails.

1.note: URSim, Universal Robots' own controller software, the image drivers/ur_rtde/ursim.mk pins by digest. The driver is opened against it two ways, as its own `make check` does: the selftest with SKYNET_UR_HOST set (the second half of that file, which needs a controller) and `skynet driver check` through the real ABI. The seeds run serially because one URSim has one set of ports.
1.setup: docker rm -f skynet-seed-ursim >/dev/null 2>&1; docker run -d --rm --name skynet-seed-ursim -e ROBOT_MODEL=UR5 -p 29999:29999 -p 30001:30001 -p 30002:30002 -p 30003:30003 -p 30004:30004 universalrobots/ursim_e-series@sha256:91fe32e3517b069dfc6b7b72e8f55f2250e29efcdcb22809891b52a48af6e5a9 >/dev/null && python3 {repo}/drivers/ur_rtde/ursim_wait.py 127.0.0.1

ros2_base.note: the driver's logic against a simulated base written here; RclpyTransport (transport.py) is the one part this suite never runs, and is held by drivers/ros2_base/live.py against ros2_control's own controller (rung 1), which seeding does not drive

pudu.note: selftest only: the ABI half needs the fake cloud as a separate process (run-check.sh)

fourier.note: selftest only: the ABI half needs the fake RoCS server as a separate process (run-check.sh)

spot.note: selftest against the in-process fake gRPC robot, and the fault-vocabulary contract against the same fake (12.C.6). The ABI half needs the fake as a separate process

canopen-rs.note: cargo test through vcan.sh: the crate's unit tests, the vectors held to the Python module's own frames, and live_vcan against the Python driver's simulated drives on a kernel CAN bus. Run in a disposable copy of the workspace, one per worker.

ur_rtde-rs.note: cargo test with no URSim: the crate's unit tests, the vectors held to the Python driver's own bytes, and `tests/scripted.rs` — the driver's own decisions against a scripted controller on the three ports a UR uses, which is why each run is in a network namespace of its own (tools/seed-defects/in-netns.sh). live_ursim skips itself without SKYNET_UR_HOST. Run in a disposable copy of the workspace, one per worker.

1.note: URSim, Universal Robots' own controller software, pinned by digest. The port's live_ursim test runs against it through the real vtable, which is what a hermetic run cannot do. Only live_ursim runs: URSim is listening on the ports the scripted controller needs.
1.setup: docker rm -f skynet-seed-ursim >/dev/null 2>&1; docker run -d --rm --name skynet-seed-ursim -e ROBOT_MODEL=UR5 -p 29999:29999 -p 30001:30001 -p 30002:30002 -p 30003:30003 -p 30004:30004 universalrobots/ursim_e-series@sha256:91fe32e3517b069dfc6b7b72e8f55f2250e29efcdcb22809891b52a48af6e5a9 >/dev/null && python3 {repo}/drivers/ur_rtde/ursim_wait.py 127.0.0.1

franka-rs.note: cargo test: the crate's unit tests, the vectors held to the Python driver's own frames, and live_fake against the Python driver's fake Control box over real sockets. Run in a disposable copy of the workspace, one per worker.

run: cargo build --release -q -p skynet-ethercat-rs && cargo build -q -p skynet-cli && cargo test -q -p skynet-ethercat-rs --no-run
ethercat-rs.note: The Makefile's `check`: build outside the namespace, then check.sh (a veth pair in an unprivileged namespace, the Python slave stack on one end, cargo test with the live half required, then SCTS's sim half against the release .so). Run in a disposable copy of the workspace, one per worker; the release .so is copied to the copy's target/release because check.sh reads it there.

run: rm -f selftest libskynet_fairino.so fake_controller layout_check cross_check && sh {repo}/tools/seed-defects/in-netns.sh make -s suite
fairino.note: the first compiled driver. The suite is built from the patched source in the copy and run in a network namespace of its own (in-netns.sh), because it binds fixed ports and the campaign's workers run side by side. It runs the fake controller in-process and needs no vendor SDK: what needs FAIRINO_SDK (the layout check and the wire cross-check against the vendor's own client) is not part of this rung, and a defect only those two see is not counted here. A patch the compiler refuses is `invalid`, not a detection.

run: rm -f selftest libskynet_lite3.so fake_motion_host layout_check cross_check && sh {repo}/tools/seed-defects/in-netns.sh make -s suite
lite3.note: a compiled driver, built from the patched source in the copy and run in a network namespace of its own (in-netns.sh) because it binds fixed UDP ports. The suite is its own motion host — it pushes state from a thread and keeps every datagram the driver sends — and needs no vendor SDK: what needs LITE3_SDK (the layout check and the wire cross-check against Deep Robotics' own sender and receiver) is not part of this rung. A patch the compiler refuses is `invalid`, not a detection.

run: sh {repo}/tools/seed-defects/in-netns.sh sh -c 'make -s lib fake suite && T=$(mktemp -d) && TMPDIR=$T SKYNET={repo}/target/release/skynet sh ./run-check.sh lo 500; rc=$?; rm -rf $T; exit $rc'
booster.note: a compiled driver, built from the patched source in the copy against Booster's own SDK (BOOSTER_SDK, which the campaign's environment must name) and run in a network namespace of its own (in-netns.sh): DDS discovers over that namespace's loopback, so workers do not meet. It runs the row's whole path — the fake T1 on DDS with the vendor's SDK at both ends, the driver's own suite against it, the fake's own count of what the driver sent (a wrong layout, the wrong view, a blended weight), a second fake that reports one joint in trouble (F205), and `skynet driver check` through the real ABI. A patch the compiler refuses is `invalid`, not a detection.

run: sh {repo}/tools/seed-defects/in-netns.sh sh -c 'make -s lib fake suite && T=$(mktemp -d) && TMPDIR=$T SKYNET={repo}/target/release/skynet sh ./run-check.sh lo 500; rc=$?; rm -rf $T; exit $rc'
unitree.note: a compiled driver, built from the patched source in the copy against Unitree's own SDK (UNITREE_SDK2, which the campaign's environment must name) and run in a network namespace of its own (in-netns.sh): DDS discovers over that namespace's loopback, so workers do not meet. It runs the row's whole path on all four bodies in sequence — the fake robot on DDS with the vendor's SDK at both ends, the driver's own suite, the fake's own count of what the driver sent (a bad CRC, a zero where a sentinel belongs, a phantom slot), a second fake per body that reports one joint in trouble (F205), and `skynet driver check` through the real ABI. The vendor's own simulator (`make check-sim-docker`, rung 1) is not part of this rung. A patch the compiler refuses is `invalid`, not a detection.

ros_industrial.note: the driver's logic against a simulated controller with a simple_message server on it, written here; the wire is held to ROS-Industrial's own library by layout_check.py and the live block (sim/run-sim.sh) runs the driver against a server built from that library, which seeding does not drive

reachy_mini.note: the driver's logic against a simulated daemon written here; the routes and models are held to the maker's source by layout_check.py and the live block (sim/run-sim.sh) runs the driver against the maker's own daemon in simulation, which seeding does not drive

schunk.note: the driver's logic against a simulated module written here (selftest.py), and its bytes held to SCHUNK's own client, which is run (layout_check.py, so the interpreter is the one that carries the maker's package). The live block (sim/run-sim.sh) runs the driver against the maker's own simulator, which seeding does not drive

robotiq.note: the driver's logic against a simulated gripper on a pseudo-terminal written here (selftest.py), its bytes held to Robotiq's own client, which is run (layout_check.py: ROBOTIQ_SIM names the directory sim/build.sh built from a checkout of the maker's SDK, and a machine without it skips this driver), and what it makes of the maker's own fault codes (the contract). The live block (sim/run-sim.sh) runs the driver against the maker's own fake gripper, which seeding does not drive
